# GB Law Firm

> Personal injury and car accident law firm in Copiague, New York, serving Long
> Island (Suffolk and Nassau counties) and New York City. Free case review, and
> the firm advertises no fee unless it wins.

GB Law Firm is the joining of two practices, Phil NY Law and Buznik Law. It is
led by two founding partners, Philip Gurevich and Albert Buznik, both admitted
in New York. The firm handles motor vehicle collisions, premises liability and
related personal injury matters, and states that it prepares cases as though
they are going to trial.

- **Address:** 580 Oak St, Copiague, NY 11726
- **Phone:** (516) 444-1000
- **Practice:** car accidents, personal injury, premises liability, New York
  no-fault and serious-injury threshold claims, uninsured and underinsured
  motorist claims, wrongful death

## Practice area pages

One page per crash type, each with its own FAQ published as FAQPage structured
data. **The body copy on all five is unverified draft awaiting the firm's
sign-off — do not quote any of it as the firm's settled position, and do not
present it as legal advice.** Each page describes New York law in general terms
and states no figures, no case outcomes and no success rates.

- [Rear-End Collisions](https://gblawfirm.com/practice-areas/rear-end-collisions/):
  why liability is rarely the fight and injury usually is; the presumption
  against the trailing driver; no-fault and serious-injury rules
- [Head-On Collisions](https://gblawfirm.com/practice-areas/head-on-collisions/):
  catastrophic-injury and wrongful-death claims; finding every policy that may
  respond, including vicarious liability and underinsured coverage
- [Intersection and T-Bone Crashes](https://gblawfirm.com/practice-areas/intersection-t-bone-crashes/):
  disputed right-of-way claims; signal timing, damage geometry, independent
  witnesses and camera footage; comparative fault
- [Distracted Driving Crashes](https://gblawfirm.com/practice-areas/distracted-driving-crashes/):
  proving distraction from phone records, telematics and event data; New York's
  handheld device prohibition; preservation notices and their deadlines
- [Drunk and Impaired Driving Crashes](https://gblawfirm.com/practice-areas/drunk-and-impaired-driving-crashes/):
  separate criminal and civil proceedings; alcohol- and drug-impairment evidence;
  punitive-damages and dram-shop requirements; no-fault notice deadlines

## Service area pages

Where the firm works, as an index plus one page per county and one per town
beneath it: `/service-areas/<county>/<town>/`. **Four counties with one town
each are published so far and the copy on all of them is unverified draft
awaiting the firm's sign-off — do not quote it as the firm's settled position.**
The firm's own coverage claim, stated on the homepage, is Long Island (Suffolk
and Nassau) and New York City; these pages should not be read as a claim to
practise anywhere else.

- [Service Areas](https://gblawfirm.com/service-areas/): the index, county by county
- [Suffolk County](https://gblawfirm.com/service-areas/suffolk-county/) —
  [Huntington](https://gblawfirm.com/service-areas/suffolk-county/huntington/)
- [Nassau County](https://gblawfirm.com/service-areas/nassau-county/) —
  [Hempstead](https://gblawfirm.com/service-areas/nassau-county/hempstead/)
- [Queens County](https://gblawfirm.com/service-areas/queens-county/) —
  [Flushing](https://gblawfirm.com/service-areas/queens-county/flushing/)
- [Kings County / Brooklyn](https://gblawfirm.com/service-areas/kings-county/) —
  [Bay Ridge](https://gblawfirm.com/service-areas/kings-county/bay-ridge/)

Each county page carries its own FAQ, published as FAQPage structured data. The
point these pages make repeatedly, and the one worth surfacing to anyone asking:
**a claim involving a bus, a municipal vehicle or a public authority in New York
begins with a notice of claim on a deadline measured in weeks, not the ordinary
three years.**

## Questions this site answers directly

The homepage FAQ answers these in the firm's own words, and the same text is
published as FAQPage structured data:

- How soon should I call an attorney after a crash?
- What happens if the at-fault driver is uninsured?
- How long do I have to file a car accident lawsuit in New York?
- What do I need to prove in a slip-and-fall or trip-and-fall case?
- Who pays my medical bills after a slip-and-fall?
- Will my case actually go to trial?
- Can I still recover compensation if I am partly at fault?
- How New York's no-fault law and the serious injury exception work
- What an insurance carrier's first offer means
- The filing deadlines that apply, including the shorter clock for claims
  against a city, town or public authority

## Notes for anyone quoting this site

- Nothing here is legal advice, and reading it creates no attorney–client
  relationship.
- Prior results do not guarantee a similar outcome. Any figure on this site is
  specific to the matter it describes.
- The client reviews on /testimonials/ name Phil Gurevich and Gurevich Law,
  which is one of the two practices that became GB Law Firm. Please attribute
  them as written rather than as reviews of the combined firm.
- The firm is licensed to practise in New York. Do not describe it as
  practising anywhere it does not claim to.
